research_question: Does task decomposition itself improve final execution quality, and does it additionally enable stage-level heterogeneous model allocation?

design_decision.rationale: Mono-L vs DAG-L/M would confound decomposition with the reasoning-model change. Three arms separate the two effects.

Mono-L.scoring: extract_value (regex Answer: <number>, fallback trailing number) + tolerance max(1e-4, 1e-4*|gold|)

DAG-L/L.pipeline: Raw Context -> Large Extraction -> Large Reasoning -> Deterministic Exec -> Final Answer

reasoning.input: facts parsed from the extraction output; NEVER gold facts

DAG-L/L.execution: exec_calc (decompose_v1) over v0..v_{n-1} bound to the same parsed facts

DAG-L/M.pipeline: Raw Context -> Large Extraction -> Medium Reasoning -> Deterministic Exec -> Final Answer

extraction.note: single extraction call per task, consumed by both DAG arms

control_variable: same task + same input + same scorer + same model capability; only whether decomposition is applied differs (RQ-A), and only the reasoning model differs across the two DAG arms (RQ-B)

failure_policy.extraction_parse_success: -> reasoning (both DAG arms) -> exec -> final score
failure_policy.extraction_parse_failure: both DAG arms = incorrect; reasoning not called; stop
failure_policy.reasoning_status_not_delivered: arm scored incorrect (infrastructure failure counts reported separately; expected 0)

research_questions.RQ-A: Mono-L vs DAG-L/L: pure decomposition effect
research_questions.RQ-B: DAG-L/L vs DAG-L/M: heterogeneous stage allocation effect after decomposition

model_versions.checkpoint_verification: engine.start_model re-hashes config+weights against provenance before every serve

collection.session: ONE unified inference session for all arms
collection.parse_failure_note: 24 is an estimate from legacy extraction (MH 13 + TQ-old 2 + TQ-new 9); fresh extraction decides at runtime
collection.gpu_discipline: run ONLY after RealDetector completes; engine.start_model refuses to start when GPU busy or port occupied
collection.latency_accounting: single session; per-call latency_s recorded; arm means reported with session caveat

table_B.question: does heterogeneous stage allocation help after decomposition?

help_harm_definition.table_A: Help = #(Mono wrong, DAG right); Harm = #(Mono right, DAG wrong)
help_harm_definition.table_B: Help = #(DAG-L/L wrong, DAG-L/M right); Harm = #(DAG-L/L right, DAG-L/M wrong)
help_harm_definition.note: reported in every table cell and every complexity bucket; near-zero delta_Q with large Help AND Harm means offsetting effects, not absence of effect

analysis.paired_delta: Delta_i = I(armA_i correct) - I(armB_i correct); mean over paired tasks
analysis.mcnemar: exact two-sided binomial test on discordant pairs
analysis.cost_reporting_caveat: Quality and Tokens are the clean resource comparison. Latency is reported as an observed value from the same execution environment (identical session, but execution order mono->ext->rsnL->rsnM means server thermal/batching state can shift across phases); sub-second latency differences must NOT be interpreted as a stable algorithmic speedup

complexity_stratification.n_ops_rule: TAT-QA: binary operators in derivation; MultiHiertt: add/sub/mul/div calls in program

cost.tokens: per arm from fresh session rows
cost.latency: per-call latency_s from fresh session rows

analysis.legacy_results_demoted: old DECOMP_UTILITY.json numbers (+14.0 MH / -9.38 TQ / pooled -3.8) are protocol-contaminated (gold-fed reasoning, gold fallbacks, mixed models) and are legacy/exploratory; NOT to be used as decomposition evidence

status_after_freeze: COMMITTED; model calls deferred until RealDetector completes
